facts.value: Computers have been used to coordinate information between multiple physical locations since the 1950s.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Computer Systems

facts.value: The U.S. military's SAGE system was the first large-scale example of such a system.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Computer Systems

facts.value: In the 1970s, computer engineers at research institutions throughout the United States began to link their computers together using telecommunications technology.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Computer Systems

facts.value: The effort was funded by ARPA (now DARPA).
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Computer Systems

facts.value: The computer network that resulted was called the ARPANET.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Computer Systems

facts.value: Logic gates are a common abstraction which can apply to most digital or analog paradigms.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Computer Systems

facts.value: The ability to store and execute lists of instructions called programs makes computers extremely versatile.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Computer Systems

facts.value: The Church–Turing thesis is a mathematical statement of this versatility: any computer with a minimum capability (being Turing-complete) is, in principle, capable of performing the same tasks that any other computer can perform.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Computer Systems

facts.value: Any type of computer (netbook, supercomputer, cellular automaton, etc.) is able to perform the same computational tasks, given enough time and storage capacity.
